title: Home
subtitle: Drag files onto the window, choose them here, or press {{shortcut}} to start a job.

dropzone.title: Drop files to print
dropzone.formatList: PDF, images (JPG, PNG, TIFF, BMP, WebP, HEIC, SVG), Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, TXT, RTF, HTML and Markdown
dropzone.folders: Folders work too — you decide whether subfolders are included.
dropzone.action: Drop files to print, or click to choose them

cli.copyFailed: Could not reach the clipboard — select the command and copy it manually.
cli.pathNote: Uses the app's full path — it is not on your PATH yet.
cli.noPathNote: Not on your PATH yet: replace {{program}} with its full path, in the app's folder.

recent.label: Recent activity
recent.empty: No recent activity yet — finished jobs will appear here.
recent.unavailable: Finished jobs live in the desktop app — run Pluryprint to see them here.
recent.errorTitle: Recent activity could not be read
recent.errorHint: Nothing was lost — the jobs are still in the desktop app.

shortcuts.label: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.hint: These work from any screen, except while you are typing in a field.
shortcuts.printFolder: Add a folder to the job
shortcuts.cancel: Cancel the current or next job
shortcuts.printNeedsFiles: Add files to the job first, then print.
shortcuts.nothingToCancel: No job is printing or waiting right now.
shortcuts.printBlocked: Fix the highlighted setting first — this job cannot be printed as it is.
shortcuts.printWaitsForFolder: Still reading a folder — print once its files are in the job.

cancelConfirm.title: Cancel this job?
cancelConfirm.message: {{file}} will stop and move to Cancelled. Pages already sent to the printer cannot be pulled back.

tip.label: Tip
tip.pathCopied: Nothing adds it to your PATH yet, so call it by its full path — the Run from CLI card copies a command that already does.
tip.pathManual: Nothing adds it to your PATH yet, so call it by its full path, in the app's folder.
tip.body: Pluryprint also prints from a script, with no window: {{command}} … runs its command-line tool, installed next to the app. {{path}} In Explorer, right-click files and choose Pluryprint; on Windows 11 the entry is under Show more options.
tip.bodyMac: Pluryprint also prints from a script, with no window: {{command}} … runs the app's own executable as a command-line tool. {{path}} In Finder, select files and choose Services › Print with Pluryprint from the right-click menu.

welcome.title: Welcome to Pluryprint
welcome.body: Open source batch printing for Windows and Mac. No 15-file limit, no Adobe required, no $149 license fee.

printers.title: Detect your printers
printers.body: We'll list every printer your system has installed — including 'Microsoft Print to PDF' if it is enabled.
printers.bodyMac: We'll list every printer your system has installed. To make a PDF instead, use Save as PDF in your apps' own print dialog.

cli.title: Print without the window
cli.body: Pluryprint has a command-line tool: {{command}} queues a batch headlessly, with stable exit codes for your scripts.

profiles.title: Pick a default profile
profiles.body: {{name}} is the default profile. Edit it, or add your own, from the Profiles screen.

ready.title: Ready to print
ready.body: Drag any number of files onto the window or press {{shortcut}}, pick a profile, and watch them queue up. In Explorer, right-click files and choose Pluryprint (on Windows 11, under Show more options).
ready.bodyMac: Drag any number of files onto the window or press {{shortcut}}, pick a profile, and watch them queue up. In Finder, right-click files and choose Services › Print with Pluryprint.
